newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.S. Gov to propose school property tax plan.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.S. Gov to propose school property tax plan.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki on Wednesday will propose a multi-year school property tax plan that vows to return a large amount of tax dollars to homeowners, according to an advance copy of his speech.

"When our school property tax plan is fully implemented, it's going to put hundreds of millions of dollars back where they belong -- in the pockets of New York's families," Pataki said in an advance copy of his State of the State address.
Pataki also promised that the school property tax plan, whose details will be disclosed next week, will cut how much the average senior citizen homeowner pays by almost half.
Further, the governor said he planned to raise financial support for schools by more than $250 million, and push to ensure that the money is not wasted on administration.

"This year, we will provide incentives for districts that follow the state's lead in reducing wasteful spending, and reward those districts that eliminate unnecessary administrative costs and concentrate their spending on children," the prepared text said.

Other highlights of the speech will focus on restoring the state's environment with $1.75 billion of funds approved by voters last November for such projects, ending parole for violent felons, and shifting welfare recipients to workfare under a bill the Administration submitted late last year.
